Approach: Native DB auditing (MySQL audit plugins / general logging)
Notes / Typical limitations: Produces logs but may not be tamper-evident; privileged DB administrators may disable/modify logging.

Captures in-DB changes, but triggers can be bypassed by privileged DB actions (e.g., disabling triggers or restoring snapshots); integrity of audit table is not guaranteed without additional protection.
Records application-visible events; does not cover direct DB-layer changes unless coupled with independent verification of persisted data.
Detects some modifications but can be recomputed by an attacker with DB write access; vulnerable when attacker can update checksum fields.

Approach: Secret-backed deterministic record fingerprinting (this work: FINGERPRINT)
Notes / Typical limitations: After each successful registry write, the service re-reads the record and separately persists one unchained HMAC data_hash row in InnoDB. A modification is detectable if it changes the normalized representation of the fixed 23-field subset and the secret remains external; coordinated same-domain deletion or rollback is not.

Approach: Per-write hash-linked audit evidence (this work: STRICT)
Notes / Typical limitations: Stores data_hash, prev_hash, and chain_hash per successful write and updates a global chain state. Retained-chain manipulation is detectable, but suffix deletion or rollback requires external expected state. The global lock serializes writes.

Buffers HMAC event rows and persists and links each completed batch of K events. Modification, removal, or reordering within retained finalized scopes is detectable; up to K − 1 pending events are volatile. Same-domain suffix deletion or rollback requires external expected state or anchoring.
Limits privileged write actions by time context for requests that traverse the configured application filter; direct database access and other bypass paths remain outside this control.
Strong tamper evidence, but operational overhead, governance, and data confidentiality constraints often complicate e-government adoption.

Approach: Application-layer architecture evaluated in this paper (per-request temporal restriction + one of FINGERPRINT / CHECKPOINT / STRICT)
Notes / Typical limitations: Combines application-path temporal restriction with secret-backed record evidence. Chained modes verify retained same-database evidence but do not independently prove completeness or freshness after coordinated deletion or rollback; external expected state or anchoring is required.
